title: Internal: handling procedure for a further notice of loss on a cover whose documented claim is still open
content:
## Applicable situation

This procedure belongs to the Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims product line. It applies to any cargo cover in the following state: a claimant reports a further loss, found in another container of a delivered shipment; the cover still carries an earlier claim that is open with its documents complete; the further loss needs a notice of its own; and that notice fails one of the grounds that can be decided as soon as a notice is registered.

A further notice that fails no such ground is not handled by this procedure; it stays open awaiting its documents.

## Outcome when the procedure is done

- The earlier claim is approved at its settlement amount, and the cover's approved-but-unpaid settlement balance is raised by that amount.
- The further notice is on file at the value the notice policy fixes, and is rejected with its controlled reason.
- The cover is in the closed-claim state, with no claim open.

## Steps

1. **Decide the open documented claim by settlement.** The desk agent approves the earlier claim with approve_claim_settlement_060ed8c3, at the amount the settlement policy fixes.
2. **Close the decided earlier claim.** The desk agent closes it with close_cargo_claim_a3572c28, on the cover of the approval.
3. **Register the further notice.** The claimant lodges the further notice in person with lodge_cargo_claim_268664bf; this step is performed by the customer themselves.
4. **Reject the further notice on its first applicable ground.** The desk agent rejects it with reject_cargo_claim_5f9631bd, on the cover the notice was lodged under, with the reason the rejection-at-registration policy fixes.
5. **Close the rejected further notice.** The desk agent closes it with close_cargo_claim_a3572c28, on the cover of the rejection.

## Who performs each step

| Step | Performed by | Business effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Desk agent | Settlement approval entry booked on the earlier claim |
| 2 | Desk agent | Cover moves to the closed-claim state |
| 3 | The customer themselves | Further notice registered; cover moves to the open-claim state |
| 4 | Desk agent | Rejection entry booked on the further notice |
| 5 | Desk agent | Cover moves to the closed-claim state |

## How each step feeds the next

```
approval (step 1) --cover reference--> first closure (step 2)
further notice (step 3) --cover reference, and the cover now in the open-claim state--> rejection (step 4)
rejection (step 4) --cover reference--> second closure (step 5)
```

## Why the order is fixed

- **Approval before the first closure.** A closure closes only a decided claim, and the approval entry is the decision. Closing first would leave an undecided claim closed; and the approval requires the cover to be in the open-claim state, which a closure would already have removed.
- **First closure before the claimant's notice.** Only one claim may be open at a time, and lodging moves the cover from the closed-claim state to the open-claim state. Lodging first would put a second claim on a cover whose claim is still open.
- **Claimant's notice before the rejection.** A rejection is booked only while the claim's cover is in the open-claim state, and the notice is the claim file the rejection decides. Rejecting first would decide nothing.
- **Rejection before the second closure.** A closure follows the decision of the open claim. Closing before the rejection would leave the registered notice undecided on a closed cover.

Every step is a synchronous action on the line's own records at the same moment: no survey, document, payment or passage of time is awaited between them.

## Ordering Q&A

**Can the claimant lodge the further notice while the earlier claim is still open, to save time?** No. Lodging first would put a second claim on a cover whose claim is still open.

**Is anything awaited between the approval and the claimant's notice?** No. The steps follow one another at the same moment.
